name: Software Freedom Conservancy
summary: US charity that takes in established free and open source software projects as part of itself. Selective and slow by its own account.

evidence.quote: The project must be exclusively devoted to the development and documentation of FOSS.
Conservancy is a 501(c)(3) charity incorporated in New York
Conservancy is a 501(c)(3) charity incorporated in New York

projects.value: Free and open source software only

evidence.quote: The project must be exclusively devoted to the development and documentation of FOSS.

gate.value: Software only, usually at least a year in development

evidence.quote: projects that have been under development for less than a year or only a "proof of concept" implementation are generally not eligible
Conservancy projects become a part of Conservancy
New Conservancy members are required to pay 10% of their revenue that Conservancy processes to Conservancy's general fund

value.note: Its pages describe donations; they don’t say who applies for grants.

evidence.quote: Member projects can receive earmarked donations through Conservancy.
paying key developers on a contractual basis to improve the project's software and its documentation

conditions.value: A licence both OSI and Debian accept

evidence.quote: all software of the project should be licensed under a license that is listed both as as an Open Source license by the Open Source Initiative and as DFSG-Free license
The project should have an existing, vibrant, diverse community that develops and documents the software.

steps.value: Short inquiry email with the project’s website

evidence.quote: New applicants should write an initial inquiry email to <apply@sfconservancy.org> with a very brief description of their project and a URL to their project's website.

steps.value: Answer its questions, then get the application

evidence.quote: We'll send back initial questions, and after those questions are answered, we'll send the full application materials.

steps.value: Evaluation committee review, over many months

evidence.quote: We do not move rapidly to accept new projects, as we have found that consideration of joining or forming a non-profit organization for your project is best done with careful consideration over a period of many months rather than rapidly.
